region.name: Pairadise
region.tagline: Storm-scrambled postcards. A Lens that can't match them.

briefing: Speck. The Bell was luck. Luck doesn't happen twice.
Pairadise claims a lens that names things nobody ever labelled. HA!
Fetch it. Read the paper. Yes, the appendix too.
reminder: Read the book, Speck. The small print. It's your size.
return: A lens with two eyes? One sees pictures, one reads words... hmph.
It just named my mug. 'A photo of a mug.' Correct. Infuriatingly correct.
Twice now, Speck. TWICE. That's not luck. That's a... pattern.
Shelf. Next to the Bell. Then go away. I need to think.

arrival: Pairadise: a postcard island. Last night's storm blew every photo off its words.
Photos here, words there. And the island's new Lens can't tell what goes with what.
resolution: The Twin Lens hums. Every photo finds its words, even ones nobody labelled.
Old Scribbit slides a tiny Twin Lens your way. 'For your giant. Postage paid.'

inhabitants.name: Mrs. Pomelo
inhabitants.role: Giver of c1 (the Pairing Net). Postmistress of the Stilt Post (house 2); her storm-unglued postcards are the Lens's training pairs.

default: Mind the puddles. Each one is a photo that lost its words.
afterSolved: Every postcard glued and posted. I may retire. I won't. But I may.

inhabitants.name: Blink
inhabitants.role: Giver of c2 (the Name Racks). Island photographer with storm photos nobody labelled and only two dabs of paint; his racks are a zero-shot classifier.

default: I snapped a hundred photos in the storm. No idea what half of them are.
Teach that Lens to match first. Mrs. Pomelo's net, up the steps!
afterSolved: Racks full, cranes apart. Even the pugs look smug.

inhabitants.name: Old Scribbit
inhabitants.role: Giver of c4 (explain). The island's old caption-writer, who writes every caption by hand, word by word: a caption-predicting model in a straw hat. The artefact appears beside him.

default: Ribbit. I write every caption by hand. Word. By. Word.
I'll be done by next spring. Or the one after.
afterSolved: I'm writing the Lens a thank-you card. Word. By. Word.

inhabitants.name: Skipper Brine
inhabitants.role: Red herring and comic relief: the ferry skipper's fix is a crate of exactly 1000 stickers, one fixed label per photo (the predetermined-categories approach the paper argues against).

default: Ahoy! I've a crate of 1000 stickers. One per photo. Job done!
Unless it's not one of my 1000 things. Then... back in the sea?
afterSolved: The Lens named a thing I've got no sticker for. Rude. Brilliant, but rude.

inhabitants.name: Kiwi
inhabitants.role: Flavour: a curious kitten full of 'why?'. Room for later fundamentals checks (cosine similarity, softmax, cross-entropy...).

default: Why do photos need words? Why is the sea wet? Why are YOU so small?
I've got SO many questions. Later. You look busy.
afterSolved: I asked the Lens 'what's this?' fifty times. It got bored. I didn't.

challenges.title: The Pairing Net

spec.title: The Pairing Net
spec.controlsHint: Drag tags · hang floats · knob + pin · 🎣
spec.rowsNote: Rows are the photos, top to bottom in 'photos' order; they never move. Columns are the 4 slots on the top rope.

cosine.note: The Lens's current cosine similarity of photo r (row, 'photos' order) with caption c (column, 'captions' order). Fixed while playing. Its row-wise favourite for the turtle photo is the 'crab' caption: it is still wrong, on purpose.

trainedCosine.note: Same layout. What the Lens has learned by the end of a winning haul (used only in the win animation).

valueGrid.note: Allowed values for the knob and the pin (both are logit multipliers). Dragging snaps to the nearest grid value; ◀ ▶ and the mouse wheel step to the neighbouring grid value.
valueGrid.format: '×' + value: 2 decimals below 1 (×0.07), 1 decimal below 20 (×14.3), otherwise an integer (×100).
valueGrid.dialMapping: log scale: angle = -135° + 270° · (log10(value) + 2) / 5, so ×0.01 sits at -135°, ×1 at -27°, ×1000 at +135°. Tick marks with numbers only at ×0.01, ×0.1, ×1, ×10, ×100, ×1000.

pin.note: null = still in its cushion (no pin on the dial).

beads.radius: r = R · (0.35 + 0.65 · p), R = the full bead radius
beads.noFloat: with no float hung, every bead is a plain grey bead of radius R·(0.35 + 0.65·max(0, cos)) (the raw similarity, no colour)

math: m = the knob value (a multiplier). order[j] = id of the caption tag in top-rope slot j.
logit[r][j] = m · cosine[r][index of order[j]]  (r = photo row, j = slot).
rowP[r][j] = exp(logit[r][j]) / Σ_k exp(logit[r][k])   (softmax along row r: the → float).
colP[r][j] = exp(logit[r][j]) / Σ_q exp(logit[q][j])   (softmax down column j: the ↓ float).
Subtract the row max (resp. column max) before exp; m goes up to 1000, so this matters.
Bead (r, j): → only: one bead coloured by rowP; ↓ only: by colP; both: a bead split vertically, left half rowP, right half colP.
Haul gauge (win animation only): L = ½·[mean_r −log rowP[r][r] + mean_j −log colP[j][j]], drawn on a 0 … ln 4 scale.
spec.rule: Section 2.3 + Figure 3: labels = arange(n), so photo i's own caption must sit in slot i (the diagonal); the loss is a symmetric cross-entropy, softmax along rows AND down columns, averaged. Section 2.5: the learned temperature τ starts at the equivalent of 0.07, i.e. the logits are multiplied by 1/0.07 ≈ 14.29 (Figure 3 multiplies by exp(t)), and is clipped so the logits are never scaled by more than 100 (Table 18: maximum temperature 100.0).
evaluation: On 🎣 Haul, run three checks. net: the top rope reads solution.captionOrder AND exactly {rows, cols} are hung (one check, one badge). start: |knob − 1/0.07| ≤ solution.startTolerance (accepts ×14.2 and ×14.3). pin: on the dial and |pin − 100| ≤ solution.pinTolerance (only ×100).
Otherwise: if the pin is missing, play the runaway animation; else play the tug. Then board.fail with the failing keys in this order: 'net', 'start', then 'pinMissing' or 'pinWrong'.
Any change to the board clears the badges. The player can haul again any number of times; nothing resets.

animations.win: 2.5 s: s goes 0 → 1; knob m(s) = start · (pin / start)^s turns by itself; cosine(s) = (1 − s²)·cosine + s²·trainedCosine; beads and the haul gauge recompute every frame (the tide drains). Then each photo slides along its row and each caption tag down its column to their diagonal knot, they flip into one postcard and fly up to a clothesline. api.sfx('ding'), then board.solve().
animations.runaway: 1.2 s: the knob spins by itself from its start value up to ×1000, beads flare to pure gold/black, the top rope snaps (api.sfx('pop')), the net droops; 1 s later it re-strings and the knob returns to the player's start value.
animations.tug: 0.4 s: the net jerks once (board.fail plays the buzz).

challenges.design: A fishing-net board of cut paper strung between two bamboo poles, spec.controlsHint along the top, ✕ top right calls api.onClose(). LEFT: four photo cards clipped to the left rope, one per row (🐢 🥥 ⛵ 🦀), fixed. TOP: four word tags pegged to the top rope (turtle, coconut, boat, crab) in spec.initialCaptionOrder; drag a tag onto another slot to swap the two (api.sfx('paper')). CENTRE: a 4×4 net; every knot is a bead whose colour and size show the Lens's current guess (spec.math, spec.beads), recomputed live after every change. A split bead (both floats hung) is two half-discs, each using its own p for colour and radius. Bead tooltip, 2 decimals, only the hung floats: '→ 0.69 · ↓ 0.34', '→ 0.69' or '↓ 0.34'; with no float hung: 'cos 0.47'. BOTTOM-LEFT: two paper floats, → and ↓ (tooltips from spec.floats); click a float to hang it on the net (→ hooks onto the right edge, ↓ onto the bottom edge) or click again to take it off. RIGHT: the Tide Knob, a big paper dial on spec.valueGrid: press anywhere on the dial and drag; the needle follows the pointer's angle (clamped to −135°…+135°) and snaps to the nearest grid value in log10 space; ◀ ▶ under it or the mouse wheel step one grid value; its value is printed under it ('×1.0'). Beside it a pin cushion holding one red pin: drag the pin onto the dial to stick it at the value under the pointer (readout '📌 ×value' beside the cushion), drag its head to move it, ◀ ▶ beside its readout step it, drag it back to the cushion (or click the cushion) to remove it. A press on the pin head grabs the pin, even where it overlaps the needle. The pin does not limit the player's own knob setting. A big 🎣 Haul button runs spec.evaluation. Win: spec.animations.win, then board.solve() (stamp + spec.successText; it calls api.onSolved() once). Failure: spec.animations.runaway (pin missing) or spec.animations.tug, then board.fail with the failing keys: each badge and its one-word title sit in the feedback line. Never show which slot a tag belongs in, never show the solution values, never say whether a value is too high or too low. From the 4th failed haul on, show spec.hintAfterFailures.text in a corner.
challenges.worldEffect: Postcards flutter up and clip onto a line between the palms: photo and words, together.
intro: The storm unglued my postcards, and the new Lens thinks turtles are crabs!
Gran's Pairing Net can teach it. Nobody remembers how she set it.
success: They're sticking! Photos to words, words to photos!
And the Lens knows a turtle from a crab. Mostly.

challenges.title: The Name Racks

spec.title: The Name Racks
spec.controlsHint: Drag a tag onto a sign · click it to wash it off

photos.art: yellow harbour crane lifting a crate
grey long-legged crane bird with a red cap, wading
the same crane bird mid-flap, mirrored
fawn boxer: tall, deep chest, square jaw, ears up, standing
brindle boxer: tall, square jaw, ears up, sitting
beige pug: small and round, flat black-masked face, curly tail
black pug: small and round, flat face, curly tail

spec.photosNote: Draw each photo as a small paper polaroid of its 'art' (no words on it). Emoji fallback: 'icon', plus a tiny 'tell' sticker in the corner when given (➰ = curly tail, so pugs never look like boxers).

embedding.note: Toy Lens. 'photos': one vector per photo. 'signs': one vector per sign TEXT, keyed '<label>|<tag id or none>'. Identical text gives the identical vector, so the two crane racks share a vector whenever their tags match. Without context, 'boxer' reads mostly as the athlete.

math: For each rack r: key = rack.label + '|' + (tag id on its sign, or 'none'); s = embedding.signs[key].
For each photo p: score[r] = cosine(embedding.photos[p], s_r) = dot / (|a|·|b|).
best = max over racks; every rack with score ≥ best − 1e-9 is tied for the top.
One top rack → the photo hangs on it. Two or more → the photo wobbles between them (⚖️) and counts as not filed.
Recompute on open and after every change.
spec.winCondition: Every photo hangs alone on the rack named by its 'truth' (no ⚖️, no ✗). Paint caps the board at 2 tags; exactly 2 settings win (spec.winningSettings), and neither has a tag that lies.
spec.rule: Section 3.1.2: the class texts are the classifier (the text encoder generates its weights), so two racks with identical sign text get identical weights and every crane photo ties between them. Section 3.1.4: polysemy (construction cranes vs cranes that fly; 'boxer' read as an athlete) is fixed by context in the prompt ('A photo of a {label}, a type of pet.'). With 2 dabs the player must see that one crane sign with its own sense splits the twins, that the boxer sign needs 'a type of pet', and that the pug sign needs nothing.

challenges.design: A bamboo wall outside Blink's shack, spec.controlsHint along the top, ✕ top right calls api.onClose(). Four racks left to right (spec.racks); the twin crane racks differ only by the little ⚓ / 🌊 painted on their posts. Each rack has a wooden sign printed with spec.signFrame (e.g. 'A photo of a crane.') and a dashed slot just before the full stop; a stamped tag prints its full 'text' in the slot ('A photo of a boxer, a type of pet.'). BOTTOM: a tray of the five stamps, each showing only its 'label' (icon + 1 word), and spec.paint paint dabs (🖌️🖌️) beside it. Drag a stamp onto a sign's slot to set it (api.sfx('stamp')): onto an empty slot it uses one dab; onto a slot that already has a tag it replaces that tag at no cost. With no dab left, a drop onto an empty slot is refused: the dabs shake, api.sfx('buzz'), nothing changes. Click a stamped tag to wash it off: its dab comes back (api.sfx('paper')). Stamps are never used up; stamped tags are not dragged sign to sign. LEFT: the Lens, a brass eye. The eight photos (spec.photos) hang on the racks chosen by spec.math and slide there (0.4 s) after every change; a rack fans out up to 8 polaroids (2 rows of 4). Tied photos wobble between their tied racks with ⚖️ and no ✗. A photo alone on a wrong rack shows a small red ✗ corner. No feedback line while playing: the marks are the feedback. Hover a photo for its four cosines, 2 decimals (boxer1 at the start: 'cos ⚓ 0.41 · 🌊 0.41 · boxer 0.42 · pug 0.50'). No submit button: when spec.winCondition holds, wait 0.6 s (any change cancels the wait), the Lens's eye turns gold, every sign glows, api.sfx('ding'), then board.solve() (stamp + spec.successText; it calls api.onSolved() once). Never suggest which tag goes where.

And it files my boxers under pug. They are NOT pugs!

challenges.title: The Two Gears
challenges.prompt:
Two numpy functions, `float64`.

### 1. `clip_loss(I_f, T_f, W_i, W_t, t)` → `float`
The pairing gear: **exactly Figure 3**, plus the pin from **Section 2.5**.
- `I_f` `(n, d_i)`, `T_f` `(n, d_t)`: photo and word features; row `k` of both is postcard `k`
- `W_i` `(d_i, d_e)`, `W_t` `(d_t, d_e)`: the linear projections
- `t`: Figure 3's learned temperature parameter, a float
- returns the mean loss, one float; finite even for a huge `t`

### 2. `zero_shot(image_emb, prompt_emb, scale=100.0)` → `(m, C)`
The naming gear: **Section 3.1.2**, prompts ensembled as in **Section 3.1.4**.
- `image_emb` `(m, d)`: photo embeddings, not unit-length
- `prompt_emb` `(C, K, d)`: `K` prompt embeddings per class, not unit-length; L2-normalise each prompt before ensembling
- `scale`: the logit scale
- returns probabilities: row `i` sums to 1 over the `C` classes
challenges.starterCode:
import numpy as np


def clip_loss(I_f, T_f, W_i, W_t, t):
    """THE PAIRING GEAR (Figure 3, with the pin from Section 2.5).

    I_f: (n, d_i) photo features   T_f: (n, d_t) word features   (row k = postcard k)
    W_i: (d_i, d_e)   W_t: (d_t, d_e)   t: float, Figure 3's learned temperature parameter
    returns: the mean loss, one float
    """
    I_f = np.asarray(I_f, dtype=np.float64)
    T_f = np.asarray(T_f, dtype=np.float64)
    # TODO: the Lens has never seen a postcard.
    return 0.0


def zero_shot(image_emb, prompt_emb, scale=100.0):
    """THE NAMING GEAR (Section 3.1.2, ensembled as in Section 3.1.4).

    image_emb: (m, d) photos   prompt_emb: (C, K, d) K prompts for each of C classes
    returns: (m, C) probabilities, each row sums to 1
    """
    image_emb = np.asarray(image_emb, dtype=np.float64)
    prompt_emb = np.asarray(prompt_emb, dtype=np.float64)
    # TODO: the Lens shrugs at every photo.
    m, C = image_emb.shape[0], prompt_emb.shape[0]
    return np.full((m, C), 1.0 / C)
challenges.tests:
import numpy as np


def _f(x):
    return float(np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64))


def _probs(x):
    return np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)


def test_two_perfect_postcards():
    I = np.eye(2)
    out = clip_loss(I, I, I, I, 0.0)
    assert np.ndim(out) == 0, "clip_loss must return one number (the mean loss), not an array"
    out = _f(out)
    assert np.isfinite(out), "clip_loss returned nan/inf for two tidy postcards"
    if abs(out - np.log(2.0)) < 1e-6:
        raise AssertionError("Every logit came out 0 when t = 0. Does the knob hold the scale itself, or its logarithm?")
    assert abs(out - 0.31326168751822286) < 1e-9, "two perfect pairs at t = 0: wrong loss"
    out2 = _f(clip_loss(I, I, I, I, np.log(2.0)))
    if abs(out2 - 0.4054651081081644) < 1e-6:
        raise AssertionError("With t = log 2 you scaled the logits by t itself. t is the logarithm of the scale.")
    if abs(out2 - 0.47407698418010663) < 1e-6:
        raise AssertionError("The knob turned the wrong way: a bigger t must make the Lens sharper, as in Figure 3.")
    assert abs(out2 - 0.1269280110429725) < 1e-9, "two perfect pairs at t = log 2: wrong loss"


def test_both_ways_round():
    I_f = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0]])
    T_f = np.array([[1.0, 0.2], [0.1, 1.0], [0.6, 1.0]])
    I = np.eye(2)
    out = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, I, I, np.log(5.0)))
    if abs(out - 0.3842139326029483) < 1e-6:
        raise AssertionError("Only the photos chose their words. The words never chose their photos.")
    if abs(out - 0.4036531743718618) < 1e-6:
        raise AssertionError("Only the words chose their photos. The photos never chose their words.")
    if abs(out - 0.7878671069748101) < 1e-6:
        raise AssertionError("Both directions are there, but the Lens counted them twice over.")
    assert abs(out - 0.39393355348740505) < 1e-9, "3 postcards at t = log 5: wrong loss"


def test_lengths_do_not_matter():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(4)
    I_f = rng.normal(size=(5, 3))
    T_f = rng.normal(size=(5, 4))
    W_i = rng.normal(size=(3, 6))
    W_t = rng.normal(size=(4, 6))
    base = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, W_i, W_t, 2.0))
    I_long = I_f * np.array([[3.0], [0.5], [7.0], [1.0], [0.2]])
    T_long = T_f * np.array([[0.1], [4.0], [1.0], [9.0], [2.5]])
    other = _f(clip_loss(I_long, T_long, W_i, W_t, 2.0))
    assert np.isfinite(base) and np.isfinite(other), "clip_loss returned nan/inf on random postcards"
    assert abs(base - _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, W_i, W_t, 0.0))) > 1e-6, "turning the knob t changed nothing"
    assert abs(base - other) < 1e-9, (
        "stretching a postcard's features changed the loss. The Lens compares directions, not lengths.")


def test_projections_are_used():
    I_f = np.array([[2.0, -2.6, 0.4], [-0.6, -0.5, -0.2], [-2.0, -0.2, -0.9]])
    T_f = np.array([[3.3, 0.2, -0.4, -0.3], [-0.7, -1.1, -0.4, 0.5], [-0.2, 1.0, -0.2, 0.0]])
    W_i = np.array([[1.5, 0.5], [-0.5, -0.2], [0.5, 1.9]])
    W_t = np.array([[-0.3, -0.2], [1.0, -0.9], [-0.3, 0.9], [0.6, 0.1]])
    out = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, W_i, W_t, 1.5))
    assert abs(out - 4.678538308532757) < 1e-9, (
        "3 postcards, d_i = 3, d_t = 4, d_e = 2, t = 1.5: wrong loss. Walk Figure 3 again, line by line.")


def test_swapping_eyes_changes_nothing():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(8)
    I_f = rng.normal(size=(6, 5))
    T_f = rng.normal(size=(6, 3))
    W_i = rng.normal(size=(5, 4))
    W_t = rng.normal(size=(3, 4))
    a = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, W_i, W_t, 1.0))
    b = _f(clip_loss(T_f, I_f, W_t, W_i, 1.0))
    assert np.isfinite(a) and np.isfinite(b), "clip_loss returned nan/inf"
    mixed = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f[::-1], W_i, W_t, 1.0))
    assert abs(a - mixed) > 1e-6, "mixing up which words go with which photo changed nothing"
    assert abs(a - b) < 1e-9, "swapping the photo side and the word side changed the loss"


def test_true_pairs_are_the_diagonal():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(15)
    I_f = rng.normal(size=(8, 4))
    T_f = I_f + 0.05 * rng.normal(size=(8, 4))
    W = np.eye(4)
    paired = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, W, W, 3.0))
    shuffled = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f[[3, 0, 6, 1, 7, 2, 5, 4]], W, W, 3.0))
    assert paired < shuffled, (
        "postcard k's photo and words are row k of each array; matching rows must cost less than mixed-up rows")
    assert paired < np.log(8.0) < shuffled, (
        "well-matched postcards must cost less than blind guessing, and mixed-up ones more")


def test_safety_pin():
    I_f = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.9848, 0.1736], [0.9397, 0.342], [0.866, 0.5]])
    T_f = np.array([[0.9986, 0.0523], [0.9903, 0.1392], [0.9135, 0.4067], [0.891, 0.454]])
    I = np.eye(2)
    huge = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, I, I, 10.0))
    assert np.isfinite(huge), "t = 10 made the loss nan/inf. Something should have stopped the knob."
    below = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, I, I, np.log(90.0)))
    if abs(huge) < 1e-6 and abs(below - 0.5034453128823664) < 1e-6:
        raise AssertionError("At t = 10 the logits ran wild. Read about the temperature in Section 2.5.")
    assert abs(below - 0.5034453128823664) < 1e-9, "4 close postcards at a scale of 90: wrong loss"
    assert abs(huge - 0.4733426872138775) < 1e-4, "t = 10: the knob stopped in the wrong place"


def test_quiet_knob_means_blind_guessing():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(23)
    I_f = rng.normal(size=(6, 3))
    T_f = rng.normal(size=(6, 3))
    W = np.eye(3)
    out = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, W, W, -30.0))
    if abs(out - np.log(6.0)) > 1e-9:
        at_zero = _f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, W, W, 0.0))
        if abs(out - at_zero) < 1e-9 and abs(_f(clip_loss(I_f, T_f, W, W, 1.0)) - at_zero) > 1e-6:
            raise AssertionError("t = -30 acted like t = 0. The pin is a ceiling, not a floor.")
    assert abs(out - np.log(6.0)) < 1e-9, "with a tiny scale every pairing looks alike: the loss must be log(6)"


def test_naming_hand_checked():
    out = _probs(zero_shot(np.array([[2.0, 0.0]]), np.array([[[1.0, 0.0]], [[0.0, 3.0]]]), scale=1.0))
    assert out.shape == (1, 2), f"1 photo and 2 classes: expected shape (1, 2), got {out.shape}"
    if np.allclose(out, [[0.8807970779778824, 0.11920292202211755]], atol=1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("Those are raw dot products. The Lens compares directions, not lengths.")
    assert np.allclose(out, [[0.7310585786300049, 0.2689414213699951]], atol=1e-9), (
        "one photo, two one-prompt classes, scale 1: wrong probabilities")


def test_names_make_probabilities():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(31)
    out = _probs(zero_shot(rng.normal(size=(5, 6)), rng.normal(size=(4, 3, 6)), scale=100.0))
    assert out.shape == (5, 4), f"5 photos, 4 classes (3 prompts each): expected (5, 4), got {out.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(out)), "zero_shot returned nan/inf"
    assert np.all(out >= 0), "probabilities can't be negative"
    assert np.allclose(out.sum(axis=1), 1.0, atol=1e-9), "each photo's probabilities must sum to 1 over the classes"
    assert not np.allclose(out, 0.25), "the Lens shrugged: every class got the same probability"


def test_scale_sharpens():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(37)
    img = rng.normal(size=(4, 5))
    prm = rng.normal(size=(3, 2, 5))
    soft = _probs(zero_shot(img, prm, scale=1.0))
    sharp = _probs(zero_shot(img, prm, scale=100.0))
    assert not np.allclose(soft, sharp), "the scale must change the probabilities"
    assert np.array_equal(soft.argmax(axis=1), sharp.argmax(axis=1)), "the scale must not change which class wins"
    assert np.all(sharp.max(axis=1) > soft.max(axis=1)), "a bigger scale must make every photo more confident"
    default = _probs(zero_shot(img, prm))
    assert np.allclose(default, sharp, atol=1e-12), "the default scale is 100"


def test_blend_the_lanterns_not_the_votes():
    prompts = np.array([[[0.766044, 0.642788], [0.819152, -0.573576]],
                        [[0.906308, 0.422618], [0.906308, 0.422618]]])
    out = _probs(zero_shot(np.array([[1.0, 0.0]]), prompts, scale=10.0))
    assert out.shape == (1, 2), f"expected shape (1, 2), got {out.shape}"
    if np.allclose(out, [[0.2461640944279006, 0.7538359055720995]], atol=1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("You blended the votes. Section 3.1.4 blends somewhere else.")
    if np.allclose(out, [[0.24285361778098247, 0.7571463822190175]], atol=1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("The blended lantern came out dim. A cosine needs unit length.")
    if np.allclose(out, [[0.19739774328434498, 0.802602256715655]], atol=1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("Only the first prompt of each class was heard.")
    assert np.allclose(out, [[0.7165480654266814, 0.2834519345733185]], atol=1e-6), (
        "two classes, two prompts each, scale 10: wrong probabilities")


def test_long_prompts_do_not_shout():
    prompts = np.array([[[5.0, 8.66025], [0.939693, -0.34202]],
                        [[0.707107, 0.707107], [0.707107, 0.707107]]])
    out = _probs(zero_shot(np.array([[0.965926, 0.258819]]), prompts, scale=10.0))
    if np.allclose(out, [[0.28074108976335305, 0.7192589102366469]], atol=1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("One long prompt drowned out the other. Normalise each prompt before you blend.")
    assert np.allclose(out, [[0.7861198215852274, 0.21388017841477264]], atol=1e-6), (
        "prompts of different lengths: wrong probabilities")


def test_photo_length_does_not_matter():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(41)
    img = rng.normal(size=(3, 4))
    prm = rng.normal(size=(5, 2, 4))
    a = _probs(zero_shot(img, prm, scale=30.0))
    b = _probs(zero_shot(img * np.array([[0.1], [6.0], [2.0]]), prm * 3.0, scale=30.0))
    assert not np.allclose(a, 0.2), "the Lens shrugged: every class got the same probability"
    assert np.allclose(a, b, atol=1e-12), "stretching photo or prompt vectors changed the answer"


def test_classes_keep_their_own_prompts():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(43)
    img = rng.normal(size=(4, 6))
    prm = rng.normal(size=(3, 5, 6))
    base = _probs(zero_shot(img, prm, scale=20.0))
    assert base.shape == (4, 3), f"4 photos, 3 classes of 5 prompts: expected (4, 3), got {base.shape}"
    shuffled_prompts = _probs(zero_shot(img, prm[:, [4, 2, 0, 3, 1]], scale=20.0))
    assert np.allclose(base, shuffled_prompts, atol=1e-12), "reordering a class's prompts must not change anything"
    swapped_classes = _probs(zero_shot(img, prm[[2, 0, 1]], scale=20.0))
    assert np.allclose(base[:, [2, 0, 1]], swapped_classes, atol=1e-12), (
        "reordering the classes must reorder the columns, nothing else")
    prm2 = prm.copy()
    prm2[0, 1] = rng.normal(size=6) * 5.0
    changed = _probs(zero_shot(img, prm2, scale=20.0))
    assert not np.allclose(base, changed), "every prompt of a class must count"

challenges.title: Why Not Write the Words?
challenges.question: Why is picking the caption faster to learn than writing it? What can my quill still do?
rubric: Why writing is hard (Section 2.3): a captioning model has to predict the exact words of the text that comes with an image, a difficult task because of the wide variety of descriptions, comments and related text that co-occur with images.

The core (Section 2.3, Figures 1 and 3): CLIP never predicts the words. It only predicts which text, as a whole, goes with which image among the candidates in a batch: the real pairs are pulled together, the other pairings pushed apart. Cosine similarity, the N × N pairings or the symmetric cross-entropy are a bonus, not required. Merely restating 'it picks instead of writes' does not count.

The evidence (Figure 2, Section 2.3): a transformer language model predicting the caption learned zero-shot ImageNet 3x slower than a baseline predicting a bag-of-words encoding of the same text, and swapping that predictive objective for CLIP's contrastive one gave a further 4x efficiency gain (≈12x overall, inferred as 3×4; the paper never states 12x). Also accept the supporting points cited in Section 2.3: contrastive objectives learn better representations than their equivalent predictive objectives, and generative models of images (Chen et al., 2020a) need over an order of magnitude more compute than contrastive models for the same performance.

What the quill can still do (Section 6, Limitations): CLIP is limited to choosing from only the concepts in a given zero-shot classifier (the captions or class names it is handed); unlike an image captioning model it cannot generate novel outputs such as a brand-new caption. Bonus: the authors suggest joint training of a contrastive and a generative objective, or searching over many natural-language explanations at inference time.
challenges.passBar: Pass if criteria 2 and 4 are clearly met plus at least one of criteria 1 or 3. Fail regardless of the count if the answer claims that CLIP writes, generates or predicts the words of captions, that the captioning objective was the more efficient one, or that CLIP can name things it is not given words for.
intro: Ribbit. Your Lens never writes a word, and still it beats me?

artefact.name: The Twin Lens
artefact.description: Two eyes: one sees photos, one reads words. Name a few things; it picks the right one.
artefact.look: A small brass spyglass (about 0.5 units long) that forks into two eyepieces: a round one framing a tiny turquoise photo, a square one framing a cream caption card with three ink lines. A glowing turquoise thread loops between the two eyes. A tiny dial with a red pin on the barrel. Idle: slow spin; the thread pulses when it is used.
